{{short description|Turkish mathematician}}
'''Betül Tanbay''' (born 1960) is a [[Turkish people|Turkish]] [[mathematician]], [[scientist]] and professor of mathematics at the [[Boğaziçi University]] in [[Istanbul]], [[Turkey]] and the first woman president of the [[Turkish Mathematical Society]] between 2010 and 2016.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/opinion/gila-benmayor/women-founded-startups-are-more-profitable-than-men-founded-ones-135360|newspaper=Hurriyet|first=Gila|last=Benmayor|title=Women-founded startups are more profitable than men-founded ones|date=3 August 2018}}</ref>

==Education==
Betül Tanbay was born in Istanbul and raised in [[Ankara]] until 1977. She graduated from the [[Lycée Janson de Sailly]], [[Paris]], [[France]] in 1978. She received her Licence en Mathématiques from  [[Louis Pasteur University|Université Louis Pasteur]], [[Strasbourg]] in 1982, and her PhD  in Mathematics under the supervision of [[Robert M. Solovay|Robert Solovay]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in the [[United States]] in 1989.<ref>[https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=32619 Record in the Genealogy Project]</ref>

==Academic career==
She has been a full time member and chairwoman in the Department of Mathematics, at Boğaziçi University, Istanbul. She has been the Vice-Provost for Foreign Affairs and represented her university at the [[European University Association]] between 2004 and 2007.<ref>[http://www.math.boun.edu.tr/index.php?option=com_content&task=section&id=26&Itemid=321 Bogazici University Vice-Provost]</ref>  She is the founding codirector of the  [[Istanbul Center for Mathematical Sciences]] (IMBM). She has been in the scientific boards of research institutes such as IMBM, [[Feza Gürsey Institute]],<ref>[http://fezagursey.boun.edu.tr/?sayfa=4 Feza Gürsey Institute Scientific Board]</ref> Institut d'Etudes Avancées - Aix Marseille (IMéRA).<ref>[http://rfiea.fr/agenda/chercheurs-la-croisee-des-disciplines-les-dynamiques-de-limera-en-perspective The dynamics of IMéRA in perspective]</ref> She was the director of a leading doctoral network project of [[Scientific and Technological Research Council of Turkey|TÜBİTAK]] between 2008 and 2012. She has worked as an executive committee member, including presidency, at the Turkish Mathematical Society;<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://euro-math-soc.eu/corporate/turkish-mathematical-society |title=Turkish Mathematical Society presidency |access-date=2018-07-21 |archive-date=2020-12-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201230124634/https://euro-math-soc.eu/corporate/turkish-mathematical-society |url-status=dead }}</ref> as delegate, Ethics Committee member, Raising Awareness Committee member,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/women-in-math/portrait/betul-tanbay |title=EMS committee memberships |access-date=2018-07-21 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180123001020/http://www.europeanwomeninmaths.org/women-in-math/portrait/betul-tanbay |archive-date=2018-01-23 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Executive Committee member at the [[European Mathematical Society]] where she was elected vice-president for the 2019-2022 period;<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://euro-math-soc.eu/committee/executive-committee |title=EMS Executive Committee |access-date=2018-07-21 |archive-date=2020-12-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201230123304/https://euro-math-soc.eu/committee/executive-committee |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://plus.google.com/+EuromathsocEurope/posts/X7wv3pfWqaC EMS vice-presidency]</ref> and as delegate, member of the Committee for Women in Mathematics at the [[International Mathematical Union]] (IMU).<ref>[https://www.mathunion.org/organization/imu-leadership-2015-2018 IMU Women in Mathematics membership]</ref> 
In 2025 she was appointed as the Chair of the Governing Board of the IMU-IDM (International Day of Mathematics).<ref>[https://www.mathunion.org/outreach/IDM IMU-International Day of Mathematics]</ref> 

===Visiting positions===
She has held visiting positions at UC Berkeley and [[University of California, Santa Barbara|UC Santa Barbara]], [[Université de Bordeaux]], [[Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu - Paris Rive Gauche|Institut de Mathématiques de Jussieu]],  [[University of Kansas]], [[Pennsylvania State University]] and joined the Kadison-Singer Conjecture Workshop at the [[American Institute of Mathematics]].

==Research areas==
Her research interests include operator algebras and set theory.

=== Representative scientific journal publications ===
* C. Akemann, J. Anderson, B. Tanbay, ''Weak Paveability And The Kadison-Singer Problem'', Journal of Operator Theory, vol. 71, no. 1, pp.&nbsp;295–300 (2014). {{ArXiv|1203.2854}} 
* B. Tanbay, A ''Letter on the Kadison-Singer problem'', Revue Roumaine des Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées, vol. 59, no. 2, pp.&nbsp;293–302 (2014). http://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2014/2/10.pdf
* C. Akemann, J. Anderson, B. Tanbay, ''The Kadison-Singer problem for the direct sum of matrix algebras'', Positivity, vol. 16, no. 1, pp 53–66 (2012). https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007%2Fs11117-010-0109-1.pdf
* C. Akemann, B. Tanbay, A. Ülger ''A Note On The Kadison-Singer Problem'', Journal of Operator Theory, vol. 63, no. 2, 363–274 (2010). {{ArXiv|0708.2366}}
